name: openssl
resume: 39 of 79 exports are checked. Hashes use hashlib. AES, RSA, Ed25519, X25519, and random bytes use the Rust crate opensslport, which calls libssl. The rest is not ported: certificates, PKCS, and PEM use the Python cryptography package. Checked read_p12, read_pubkey, rsa_sign, and write_pem. Reserved decrypt_envelope, ecdsa_parse, and pkcs7_decrypt.

functions.name: sha256
functions.done: SHA-256 hex digest from hashlib.

check.case: sha256 of foo

proof.r:
.libPaths(c(path.expand("~/R/library"), .libPaths()))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(openssl))
one <- function() {
  as.character(sha256("foo"))
}
value <- one()
elapsed <- numeric(20)
for (i in seq_len(20)) {
  t0 <- as.numeric(Sys.time())
  one()
  elapsed[[i]] <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) - t0
}
shown <- enc2utf8(paste(as.character(value), collapse = "|"))
shown <- gsub("\n", " / ", shown, fixed = TRUE)
cat("VALUE ", shown, "\n", sep = "")
cat(sprintf("MS %.17g\n", median(elapsed) * 1000))

proof.python:
import statistics
import time
from openssl import sha256, aes_ctr_encrypt, aes_ctr_decrypt

def one():
    key = bytes.fromhex(sha256("This is super secret"))
    iv = bytes(range(1, 17))
    y = aes_ctr_encrypt(b"hello curl", key, iv)
    return aes_ctr_decrypt(y, key, iv).decode()

value = one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
if isinstance(value, bool):
    shown = "TRUE" if value else "FALSE"
elif value is None:
    shown = "NULL"
else:
    shown = str(value).replace("\n", " / ")
print("VALUE " + shown)
print(f"MS {statistics.median(elapsed):.17g}")
